title: Where do pronouns go?
topic: pronouns with the infinitive, the gerund and the imperative
why: After indirect and double pronouns, this lesson settles where they go with the infinitive, the gerund and the imperative, and above all the written accent that appears when they attach to the verb (dímelo, comprándolo, dártelo). It lets the learner ask for help and give instructions naturally, just before the big pronoun review.

{"lessons": ["

With an infinitive: two possible positions

With a single conjugated verb, you already know the pronoun goes in front: Lo compro. But with ir a, querer, poder, tener que, deber + infinitive, Spanish gives you a choice:

Before the conjugated verbAttached to the infinitiveTranslation
Lo voy a comprar.Voy a comprarlo.I'm going to buy it.
La quiero ver.Quiero verla.I want to see her.
Te puedo ayudar.Puedo ayudarte.I can help you.
Me tengo que duchar.Tengo que ducharme.I have to take a shower.
Le debes escribir.Debes escribirle.You should write to him (or her).

Both sentences are correct and mean the same thing. Careful: attached means attached, as one single word: comprarlo, not \"comprar lo.\"

What's impossible

  • The pronoun never goes between the two verbs: voy lo a comprar doesn't exist.
  • It never goes right before a separate infinitive: voy a lo comprar is wrong.
  • Two pronouns stay together: Te lo voy a dar or Voy a dártelo, never one pronoun on each side (te voy a darlo is wrong).

The accent that appears

With one pronoun attached to the infinitive, no accent: comprarlo, verla, decirte. With two pronouns, the word gets longer and the stressed syllable becomes the third from the end: you write the accent. dar → dártelo, decir → decírselo, explicar → explicártelo.

", "

With the gerund: leyéndolo

Same freedom with estar or seguir + gerund (the \"-ing\" form): the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb, or attaches to the gerund.

BeforeAttached to the gerundTranslation
Lo estoy leyendo.Estoy leyéndolo.I'm reading it.
La estamos arreglando.Estamos arreglándola.We're fixing it.
Me estoy duchando.Estoy duchándome.I'm taking a shower.
Se lo estoy explicando.Estoy explicándoselo.I'm explaining it to him (or her).

Here, you need a written accent from the very first pronoun. Why? The gerund is stressed on -an- or -en- (comprando, leyendo). Add a syllable, and that vowel becomes the third from the end: com-prán-do-lo. In Spanish, a word stressed there always carries a written accent.

Say the word out loud: the stress never moves. You say comPRANdo, so comPRÁNdolo. The written accent is simply there to show it once the word gets longer.

Accent summary

FormOne pronounTwo pronouns
infinitivecomprarlo (no accent)comprártelo
gerundcomprándolocomprándotelo
tú imperativecómpralocómpratelo

And if you can't decide between the two positions, remember that putting the pronoun before the conjugated verb is always possible and avoids accents: Lo estoy leyendo.

", "

In the imperative: dímelo, cómpralo, siéntate

In the affirmative imperative, there's no choice: the pronouns attach to the end of the verb, a bit like English \"tell me,\" but as one single word and always in the order indirect + direct: dímelo = \"tell-me-it,\" i.e. tell it to me.

Verb + pronoun(s)túustedTranslation
comprar + locómpralocómprelobuy it
ayudar + meayúdameayúdemehelp me
sentarsesiéntatesiéntesesit down
decir + me + lodímelodígamelotell it to me
dar + me + lodámelodémelogive it to me
dar + se + lodáselodéselogive it to him / her
poner + loponlopóngaloput it (there)
hacer + lohazlohágalodo it
traer + me + lotráemelotráigamelobring it to me

The accent: a simple rule

  • One-syllable verb + one pronoun: no accent (dime, hazlo, ponlo, dale).
  • In every other case, write an accent on the verb's stressed syllable: cómpralo, llámame, siéntate, dímelo, dáselo.

Handy for asking for help or giving instructions:

¿Las cajas? Súbelas al tercero, por favor.The boxes? Take them up to the third floor, please.
Rellene el formulario y fírmelo aquí.Fill out the form and sign it here.

In the negative, which you'll learn later, the pronouns move back in front of the verb (no lo compres). For now, just remember the affirmative.
